h1:
Lopburi in 3 Days, 2 Nights
Old Town, Nature & Cafes
intro: Lopburi sits just over two hours from Bangkok, but inside it you'll find an old town from the reign of King Narai, monkeys that have lived alongside people for so long they've become the city's mascot, a huge dam across the Pa Sak River, and sunflower fields glowing yellow toward the end of the year. Three days and two nights is just enough to fit all three sides of the city without rushing. We've mapped out the timing for the whole trip, with real places to eat and a rough budget to go with it.

blocks.html: This plan is built for people driving themselves, because Lopburi's sights are spread between the old town and Phatthana Nikhom district about 40 km away. If you come by train you can do the old town easily since the station sits right in the middle of town, but for the dam and the sunflower fields you'll want to rent a car or hire a songthaew. We've ordered the days so you start with the walkable old town on day one, then head out to nature the day after.

blocks.title: Read before you plan
blocks.html: The sunflowers only bloom from late November to mid-January. Come at any other time and the fields are just bare plots. This plan still works year-round — just skip the day-2 sunflower slot and spend longer at the dam and the cafes instead.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old Town, Monkeys & King Narai's Palace

blocks.html: Take day one at an easy walking pace inside the old town. The main sights are all close together, within a few hundred metres of each other. Start with the city's landmark.

items.activity: Arrive in Lopburi, check in at a hotel in the old town, drop your bags and head out on foot
items.note: A place to stay in the old town puts you within walking distance of every sight and saves time finding transport

items.activity: Prang Sam Yot — three Khmer towers in a row, around 800 years old, the symbol of Lopburi
items.note: Entry around 10 THB for Thais · There are a LOT of monkeys here — tuck away glasses, hats and plastic bags, and don't walk in carrying a bag of food

items.activity: San Phra Kan Shrine — across the road from Prang Sam Yot, just a quick walk over. It's an old shrine where the monkeys live in the highest density in the city
items.note: This is the real home of Lopburi's monkey troop — keep a close eye on your valuables

items.activity: Kuaytiao Ruea Ayutthaya (the 'boat noodles in town' spot) — a hidden shop about 200 m from Prang Sam Yot, around 15 THB a bowl
items.note: Opens around 09:00, closed Fridays · Order several bowls easily since they're small

items.activity: King Narai's Palace (Phra Narai Ratchaniwet) — the palace King Narai built as his second capital. Walk the walls, throne halls and the museum inside the palace grounds
items.note: Entry around 30 THB · Not much shade, so bring a hat and water. Allow about 1.5–2 hours to walk through

items.activity: Ban Wichayen — the house of a Greek nobleman in King Narai's era, with mixed European-Thai-Persian architecture, a few minutes' walk from the palace
items.note: The old brick ruins photograph well in the soft afternoon light

items.activity: Stroll the old streets around the Sa Kaeo roundabout to find dinner and dessert
items.note: Lopburi is known for khanom piakpoon (a coconut jelly dessert) and fresh milk — stop by one of the old fresh-milk shops in town

blocks.title: What to know about the monkeys
blocks.html: Lopburi's monkeys are smart and fast. They watch for food and anything shiny, so if you walk past carrying a plastic bag or a water bottle there's a good chance one grabs it. Use a zip bag, take off your sunglasses and put them away, and don't hand over food — you'll get swarmed instantly.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Pa Sak Dam, Sunflower Fields & Farm Cafes

blocks.html: Today you head out of town toward Phatthana Nikhom district, where Lopburi's nature sights cluster together — Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, the Khao Chin Lae sunflower fields, and several farm cafes along the same route. It's about a 45-minute to one-hour drive from the city centre.

items.activity: Leave town early, heading for Phatthana Nikhom district
items.note: Set off early so you reach the sunflower fields between 8 and 10 am, when the sun isn't harsh yet and the flowers face the light

items.activity: Khao Chin Lae sunflower fields — the largest in Lopburi, with mountains and the white Wat Weluwan as a backdrop, plus a tram ride around the field and photo arches
items.note: Only blooms late Nov–mid Jan · Outside the season, skip ahead and spend longer at the dam and cafes

items.activity: Pa Sak Jolasid Dam — the longest earthen dam in Thailand. Walk along the dam crest for views over the reservoir stretching as far as you can see; you can also take the dam's tram
items.note: The highlight is the railway that runs over the water above the dam — with good timing you'll see a train cross the reservoir

items.activity: Lunch at a farm cafe near the dam entrance, such as Baan Kluay Lae Khai Cafe or 81 Cafe & Bistro
items.note: The cafes around here have a countryside feel — gardens, rice fields, ponds — and serve main dishes too, at gentle prices

items.activity: Keep relaxing and taking photos at the cafe, or stop at the Phatthana Nikhom viewpoint overlooking the Pa Sak reservoir
items.note: By late afternoon the light softens — a good time to shoot the fields and mountain views

items.activity: If you still have the energy, loop back to the sunflower fields for the evening light, 15:00–17:00, to capture another round
items.note: Evening light is softer than the morning — great for backlit shots of the flowers

items.activity: Head back into town for dinner — try tom yum boat noodles with shrimp paste, or a local restaurant in town
items.note: The drive back into town is about an hour; leave extra time for heavier evening traffic

blocks.text: Day 3 — Old-Town Cafes, Souvenirs, Then Home

blocks.html: Take the last day slow, no rush. Pick up the smaller sights in town you haven't seen yet, sit in an old-town cafe, buy some souvenirs, then head home in the afternoon.

items.activity: Check out and leave your bags at the hotel first
items.note: So you can keep exploring without dragging luggage around

items.activity: Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat Lopburi — the main Lopburi-era prang near the train station. Walk quietly among the old ruins
items.note: Less crowded than Prang Sam Yot, with photos that come out lovely and calm

items.activity: Sit in an old-town cafe such as Layer Lopburi or The Mellow Cafe — coffee and bakery
items.note: The town cafes lean minimalist white-and-brown, with house-made croissants and bakery

items.activity: Lunch at a local spot, or go back to a favourite boat-noodle shop one more time
items.note: Try a place you didn't get to on day one

items.activity: Buy souvenirs — Lopburi is known for custard apples, khanom piakpoon, and local dried goods
items.note: Custard apples are only sweet in season (around Jul–Sep); other times go for dried snacks instead

items.activity: Pick up your bags at the hotel and travel home
items.note: If you're taking the train, Lopburi station is right in the middle of town and easy to walk to

blocks.text: Places to actually eat on this trip

blocks.html: Lopburi's food is mainly boat noodles, tom yum noodles, and local desserts like khanom piakpoon and fresh milk. These are the spots locals go to and that reviews bring up often, ordered by how easily they fit into this plan.

items.name: Kuaytiao Ruea Ayutthaya (boat noodles in town)
items.blurb: A hidden shop in the old town about 200 m from Prang Sam Yot — small bowls, rich broth, and easy to order several. Locals have eaten here for years.
items.meta: Old town · opens around 09:00 · closed Fri

items.name: Thong Thae Wagyu Boat Noodles, Lopburi branch
items.blurb: An upgraded take on boat noodles — wagyu, ribeye, kurobuta pork and hot pot. Good for a day you want something more substantial.

items.name: Chaloem Thai Tom Yum Noodles
items.blurb: A tom yum noodle shop on the roadside near Wat Phrommat, with a vintage feel and a bold tom yum broth. Good for dinner before heading back to the hotel.

items.name: Saep Ver Tom Yum Noodles with Shrimp Paste
items.blurb: Rich tom yum noodles with shrimp paste, across from the Jom Phon golf course. Open midday to afternoon — handy to stop at on the way out of town.

items.name: Baan Kluay Lae Khai Cafe
items.blurb: A farm cafe on the way to Pa Sak Dam, with flower gardens, photo corners, and main dishes at gentle prices. Good for lunch on day 2.

items.name: 81 Cafe & Bistro
items.blurb: A loft-style countryside cafe before you reach Pa Sak Dam, surrounded by rice fields, a vegetable garden and a pond, with plenty of spots to relax and shoot photos.

items.name: Layer Lopburi
items.blurb: A town cafe in minimalist white-and-brown tones with good coffee and house-made croissants and bakery. Good for a morning sit on your last day before heading home.

items.name: The Mellow Cafe
items.blurb: A coffee shop in town with coffee, drinks, bakery and ice cream in a warm, easy setting. Good for an afternoon break.

blocks.html: Lopburi's hotels are spread across two zones. For a three-day trip like this, staying in the old town is the best value, since you can walk to the day-one and day-three sights and only drive out to nature on day two.

items.name: Old town (around the Sa Kaeo roundabout–train station)
items.blurb: Close to Prang Sam Yot, King Narai's Palace and the old restaurants. Walkable, and ideal if you arrive by train.

items.name: New town (Narai Maharat Road)
items.blurb: Newer hotels, with malls and convenience stores all around. Good if you're driving yourself and want a more comfortable, convenient base.

blocks.title: Rough budget
blocks.html: Three days and two nights on a budget: 2 nights' accommodation around ฿1,000–2,000 · food over 3 days around ฿900–1,500 per person · entry fees totalling no more than ฿200 · fuel or a hired songthaew to the dam and sunflower fields around ฿800–1,500 for the pair. All in, that's roughly ฿3,500–6,000 per person.

faq.q: Do you need your own car to travel around Lopburi?
faq.a: Not for the old town on day one — the sights are close together and walkable, and the train station is right in the middle of town. But for Pa Sak Jolasid Dam and the sunflower fields in Phatthana Nikhom district, you'll want to rent a car or hire a songthaew, since they're about 40 km out of town and public transport is sparse.

faq.q: When do the Lopburi sunflowers bloom?
faq.a: The Khao Chin Lae sunflower fields bloom from late November to mid-January. The best time for photos is 08:00–10:00, when the sun isn't harsh and the flowers face the light, or in the evening light from 15:00–17:00. Outside the season the fields are just bare plots — go to the dam and the cafes instead.

faq.q: Are the Lopburi monkeys dangerous? What should you watch out for?
faq.a: The monkeys aren't aggressive, but they're smart and fast. They watch for food and anything shiny, so keep your sunglasses, hat and valuables in a zip bag, don't walk past carrying a plastic bag or water bottle, and don't hand over food — you'll get swarmed instantly. The spots with the most monkeys are Prang Sam Yot and San Phra Kan Shrine.

faq.q: What can you do in Lopburi in 3 days and 2 nights?
faq.a: This plan splits into the old town on day one (Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan Shrine, King Narai's Palace, Ban Wichayen), nature on day two (Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, the Khao Chin Lae sunflower fields, farm cafes), and old-town cafes plus souvenir shopping on the last day — covering culture, nature and cafes all together.

faq.q: How far is Lopburi from Bangkok, and how do you get there?
faq.a: Lopburi is about 150 km from Bangkok, roughly a 2.5-hour drive, or you can take the northern-line train to Lopburi station, which sits right in the middle of the old town. It's a good fit for a weekend trip when you don't want to drive far.
